generatedCommentsNodes.comment: The changes to make certain methods public (`getSystemIndexDescriptors`, `getSystemResourceDescriptors`) and override others (`isExternal`, `getAllowedElasticProductOrigins`, etc.) are consistent with the new design. Ensure that these changes do not break any existing functionality.

The removal of `featureName`, `origin`, and `owningFeature` from `SystemIndexMigrationInfo` and their introduction in `SystemResourceMigrationInfo` is a significant change. However, the methods that were using these fields directly in `SystemIndexMigrationInfo` (like `getFeatureName()`, `getOrigin()`, and `createClient(Client baseClient)`) are being overridden or re-implemented in `SystemDataStreamMigrationInfo`. This could lead to confusion if not all subclasses of `SystemResourceMigrationInfo` implement these methods. Ensure that all subclasses properly override these methods to avoid runtime errors.

The removal of `IndexPatternMatcher.getMatchingIndices(Metadata metadata)` from `IndexPatternMatcher` and its addition to a new interface `IndexMatcher` is correct but could be improved for clarity. The method signature and documentation should remain consistent between the old and new interfaces to avoid confusion.

The method `needsToBeMigrated` (renamed to `needToBeMigrated`) now takes a `Stream<IndexMetadata>` instead of a single `IndexMetadata`. This change is logical given the new context, but ensure that all callers of this method are updated accordingly and that the stream is properly handled.

The addition of the `includeSystem` parameter in several methods (`reindexRequired`, `getReindexRequiredPredicate`) is a logical extension. Ensure that all calls to these methods are updated accordingly, especially those in tests and other parts of the codebase that might rely on the previous signature.

The update in the documentation of `SystemIndices` to reflect the change from `SystemIndexDescriptor` and `SystemDataStreamDescriptor` to `SystemResourceDescriptor` is necessary. Ensure that all references to these classes in the documentation are updated accordingly.

The `SAME_CLASS_COMPARATOR` in `SystemResourceMigrationInfo` now compares using `getCurrentResourceName()` instead of `getCurrentIndexName()`. This change might affect the sorting and comparison logic if subclasses like `SystemDataStreamMigrationInfo` do not correctly implement `getCurrentResourceName()`. Ensure that all subclasses provide a meaningful implementation for this method.

The introduction of `SystemResourceDescriptor` and its implementation in `SystemIndexDescriptor` and `SystemDataStreamDescriptor` is a significant change. Ensure that all existing implementations of these classes are updated to implement `SystemResourceDescriptor`. Also, verify that the new methods (`getOrigin`, `isAutomaticallyManaged`, etc.) do not introduce any unintended side effects.

The addition of the `makeSystem` parameter in `prepareBackingIndex` is a logical extension. Ensure that all calls to this method are updated accordingly, especially those in tests and other parts of the codebase that might rely on the previous signature.

The removal of `isInternal()` and its replacement with checks on `isExternal()` is consistent with the new design. However, ensure that all parts of the codebase that rely on `isInternal()` are updated to use the appropriate method (`isExternal()`) or logic.

The refactoring of `getRestoreFromSnapshotAffectedResources` to use `getSystemResourceDescriptors` instead of separate methods for indices and data streams is a good step towards simplification. Ensure that this change does not inadvertently exclude any system resources from being considered in the snapshot restoration process.

In `cancelExistingDataStreamMigrationAndRetry`, the error message is constructed using string concatenation. It would be more readable and maintainable to use `Strings.format` or similar formatting methods provided by Elasticsearch.
In `cancelExistingDataStreamMigrationAndMarkAsFailed`, the method also constructs an error message using string concatenation. Similar to the previous comment, it is recommended to use a formatting method for better readability and maintainability.
In `migrateDataStream`, the error message in the catch block uses string concatenation. It is advisable to use a logging method that supports parameterized messages to avoid potential performance issues with string concatenation.
In `checkDataStreamMigrationStatus`, the exception message could be improved by including more details about the specific errors encountered during the migration process.
In `dataStreamMigrationFailed`, the exception message is constructed using string concatenation. It is recommended to use a logging method that supports parameterized messages for better readability and maintainability.

In the `run` method, the check for closed indices uses `getCurrentResourceName()` which might not be appropriate if the resource is not an index. Ensure that `isCurrentIndexClosed()` correctly identifies whether a resource (index or data stream) is closed.

Could this go into an infinite recursive loop if another part of the system is causing persistent errors? e.g. `migrateDataStream()` -> `checkDataStreamMigrationStatus()` -> `cancelExistingDataStreamMigrationAndRetry()` ->  `cancelDataStreamMigration()` -> `migrateDataStream()` -> ...
(I may be missunderstanding the flow control here)

In the original system index migration logic, an error would just stop the whole migration from continuing, such that a user would need to retry.  I spoke with @gwbrown, who mentioned that this was intentional in case there was a failure elsewhere in the system.  WDYT?

It shouldn't. The chain `migrateDataStream()` -> ... -> `cancelExistingDataStreamMigrationAndRetry()` is possible if a task for migrating that data stream already exists and is in a failed state. In that case, we cancel it and start a new one.
A new task is only started if the cancellation is successful. This means we shouldn't receive a `ResourceAlreadyExistsException` (line 649), which means that `checkDataStreamMigrationStatus` is called with `restartMigrationOnError=false` (line 647).

There is still slight possibility that we end up at the line 714 not because of exception from `dataStreamMigrationFailed` (lines 701 and 703), but because of another error, I will try to improve handling there.

>an error would just stop the whole migration from continuing

Logic here is similar to deleting existing index created during failed migration attempt

> Logic here is similar to deleting existing index created during failed migration attempt

Yeah that makes sense and it's a good idea to retry.  

>There is still slight possibility that we end up at the line 714 not because of exception from dataStreamMigrationFailed (lines 701 and 703), but because of another error, I will try to improve handling there.

Exactly.  I'm worried that an issue in some other part of ES might cause this to just loop forever.

Should be fixed now
Thanks for renaming this to something sensible
Should this be at the warn level?

I don't think so. This code should only execute in one scenario: the migration of a data stream starts -> the [child task](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/8.x/x-pack/plugin/migrate/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/migrate/task/ReindexDataStreamPersistentTaskExecutor.java#L52) migrating the data stream fails for some reason -> the user restarts the system indices migration task.

Since the data stream migration task [retains](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/8.x/x-pack/plugin/migrate/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/migrate/task/ReindexDataStreamPersistentTaskExecutor.java#L295) its status for 1 day, we need to "cancel" the existing task and start a new one to avoid getting the same failure result again. In this case, the failure has already been logged.
"Canceling" the task here is part of normal operation, so I don't think it should be logged as error or warning.  I don't even want to make it info as it might be confusing to see
